screening_decisions.reason: Study uses intravenous (IV) clomipramine administration, not oral administration as required by selection criteria. While it is an RCT with adolescents (age 16.2) and a TCA, the route of administration does not match the inclusion criteria.
Study investigates fluoxetine, which is an SSRI (selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor), not a tricyclic antidepressant. The selection criteria specifically require tricyclic drugs.
RCT comparing nortriptyline (TCA) with placebo in adolescents aged 12-17 years with major depressive disorder. Oral administration (implied by plasma level monitoring). Meets all selection criteria.
This is a qualitative review article, not a randomized controlled trial. Selection criteria require RCTs.

Double-blind placebo-controlled trial of imipramine (TCA) in depressed children. Oral administration implied. Age range appears to be prepubertal children (within 6-18 years). Meets selection criteria despite small sample size.

Randomized, double-blind crossover study of amitriptyline (TCA) vs placebo in children aged 9-12 years with major depressive disorder. Oral administration (1-2.5 mg/kg/day). Meets all selection criteria.
This is a Cochrane review about newer generation antidepressants (SSRIs), not a primary RCT. Additionally, the focus is on SSRIs, not tricyclic drugs.

RCT comparing imipramine (TCA) + CBT vs placebo + CBT in adolescents with comorbid anxiety and major depressive disorders. Oral imipramine. Depression is a comorbid condition. Meets core criteria - conservative inclusion.

Double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT of imipramine (TCA) in prepubertal children with major depressive disorder. Oral administration (up to 5 mg/kg/d). Age range likely within 6-18 years. Meets all selection criteria.

RCT with three arms: paroxetine, imipramine (TCA), and placebo. The imipramine vs placebo comparison meets selection criteria. Adolescents with major depression. Oral administration. Conservative inclusion due to presence of qualifying TCA arm.
This is a review/discussion paper about mechanisms of action of antidepressants, not a clinical RCT. Does not meet selection criteria.
This is a review of SSRI overdose safety, not an RCT of TCA treatment for depression. Does not meet selection criteria.
This is a methodological paper about meta-analysis inconsistency, not a clinical RCT. Does not meet selection criteria.

This study examines amitriptyline poisoning/intoxication cases, not treatment of depression. The population is not depressed patients receiving therapeutic treatment. Does not meet selection criteria.

Analysis of drug vs placebo response rates in children with depression, appears to be from an RCT comparing tricyclic treatment to placebo. Children with depression. Conservative inclusion as it appears to contain data from a qualifying trial.
RCT comparing desipramine (TCA) with placebo in adolescents aged 13-18 years with major depression. Oral administration. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a review/discussion paper about the current status and future directions of psychopharmacology research, not an RCT. Does not meet selection criteria.

Double-blind, placebo-controlled study comparing imipramine (TCA) with placebo. Depression rating scales were used as outcomes. Conservative inclusion as depression is mentioned as an outcome measure.

This study examines unintentional TCA ingestions/poisoning in children, not treatment of depression. The population is not depressed patients receiving therapeutic treatment. Does not meet selection criteria.
RCT comparing amitriptyline (TCA) with placebo in adolescents aged 12-17 years with major depressive disorder. Oral administration (5 mg/kg per day). Meets all selection criteria.
Double-blind trial of clomipramine (TCA) in children with school refusal. Depression relief mentioned as an outcome (rapid relief of depression). Conservative inclusion as depression is mentioned.
This is a meta-analysis, not a primary RCT. Additionally, patients are aged 18-65 years, outside the 6-18 year age range specified in selection criteria.
Study of imipramine (TCA) treatment in prepubertal children aged 7-12 years with major depressive disorder. Oral administration implied. Depression outcomes measured. Meets selection criteria.
RCT comparing amitriptyline (TCA) with placebo in adolescents with treatment-resistant major depressive disorder. Oral administration. Meets all selection criteria.

8-week double-blind study of imipramine (TCA) vs placebo in anxious-depressed adolescents. Oral administration. While primary outcome is compliance, it is from an RCT with TCA vs placebo in depressed adolescents. Conservative inclusion.
